content.content:
The page doesn't document most of the options you listed. It covers these `web()` options:

- **`headers`**: Sent only to the target's site, for protected previews or tunnel warning pages. Setting it turns off the browser's HTTP cache and blocks service workers.
- **`basicAuth`**: Takes `username` and `password`. Use `secrets.get(name)` for the password so the runner keeps it out of reports and logs.
- **`viewport`**: Sets the initial size in pixels (default 1280 by 720). `viewport: null` leaves the page to fill the window.
- **`browser`**: Selects the engine, for example `'webkit'`.
- **`screencast`**: Takes `size` to fix the video size. Without it, a video keeps the size the page had when recording started.

The page doesn't mention **launch args**, **persistent profile / `userDataDir`**, **extensions**, **`connectOverCDP`** or an existing browser, **`storageState`**, **init scripts**, or **trace**. For those, check the [Web engine reference](https://e2e.tester.army/docs/reference/web), which lists every `web()` option, and the [Working with the browser](https://e2e.tester.army/docs/browser) guide.

**Plans and pricing**

| Plan | Price | Test runs | Concurrent runs | Projects | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Free** | $0 | 5 | 1 | 2 | No credit card required |
| **Hobby** | $99/mo | Up to 250 | 3 | 2 | Adds GitHub, Slack, and webhook integrations |
| **Startup** | $299/mo | Up to 1,000 | 10 | 5 | Labeled "most popular"; includes everything in Hobby |
| **Enterprise** | Custom | Custom | Custom | Custom | Booked via a sales call |

All plans include unlimited members and web and mobile testing support. Yearly billing is offered with a 15% discount.

**Limits and usage**

- A test run counts as one run, whether triggered from chat, the CLI, a GitHub deployment, or a scheduled job, with up to 20 minutes of execution time.
- When the quota is reached, new runs are blocked until it resets on the 1st of the next month. You can upgrade or contact the company to raise the limit.

**Enterprise**

Enterprise includes everything in Startup, plus SLA support via Slack Connect, white-glove onboarding, strategic feature partnership, SSO/SAML, and custom integrations. The FAQ says it also covers custom limits, self-hosting, and dedicated support.

**Not stated on the page**

- Data retention policies.
- Self-hosting details beyond the FAQ mention, such as availability, requirements, or pricing.

**Cancellation**

You can cancel anytime from dashboard settings. The subscription remains active until the end of the billing period.

**Launch HN: TesterArmy (YC P26)**. The page shows a "4 months ago" timestamp rather than an exact date, and the post had 132 points.

**Founders:** Oskar, Szymon, and Piotr, who are based in Poland. The commenter "okwasniewski" answered most questions.

**Product:** An agentic testing platform for web and mobile apps. Users write tests in natural language, and agents run them before deployment and in production. The team describes it as "fully built around agents," with a CLI that lets a coding agent manage tests, GitHub integration, and Slack or Discord alerts. Per the founders, it uses a hybrid of vision and accessibility APIs, supports Chromium, iOS, and Android, and plans iPadOS support. Non-iOS Apple platforms aren't supported yet.

**Criticisms and questions, with founder answers:**

- **Why not let an LLM write E2E tests?** Founders said static tests are brittle, depend on selectors and wait times, and struggle with dynamic content like AI chat. They also cited the cost of auth, OTP email handling, captchas, and recordings. One commenter said in-house testing with Claude or Codex was easier for them.
- **Cost vs. deterministic tests:** A commenter cited $300 per 1K tests (about $0.30 each) and compared it with Playwright MCP's token usage. Founders said they have done extensive context engineering and cache agent trajectories, but not full test runs, to keep the agent in the loop.
- **Stability and nondeterminism:** Founders said they use "harness engineering," inject previous test trajectories, and split tests into smaller steps to limit context overload.
- **Model choice and timeouts:** Founders chose Gemini 3 Flash for cost reasons and said they would update models when a better cost-fit option appears. They did not clearly address the 15-minute hard timeout.
- **Speed:** A commenter reported about 3 minutes for a basic booking.com test.
- **Benchmarks:** Founders said they have none yet and focus on customer experience.
- **Security and third-party SaaS:** Commenters were wary of outsourcing testing. Founders said the product can run from just a URL or mobile build, without codebase access.
- **Pricing:** Commenters questioned usage limits on the hobby plan. Founders said self-serve plans cover lower usage and larger needs require a call.
- **Mobile state and auth:** One commenter asked how auth state persists across cold starts and device reboots. No answer appears in the thread.
- **Captchas and human review:** A commenter asked about Cloudflare Turnstile and whether humans are in the loop. Founders mentioned handling captchas as part of their infrastructure but did not address human review.
- **Competitors:** Commenters raised Revyl, mobileboost, Rainforest QA, and TestingBot. Founders said they support web and mobile with one agent and that Revyl is vision-only, which they called slower. They did not respond to the Rainforest comparison.
- **Physical devices:** A TestingBot commenter asked whether simulators and emulators count as real devices. The founders did not directly answer.
- **Domain:** Commenters advised moving from .army to .com to avoid spam filtering. Founders said they own the .com and plan to migrate.
- **Other comments:** Several commenters promoted an open-source alternative, agent-qa, and one accused the author of spamming it. Others were skeptical that YC would fund this in 2026. The thread also had a tangent about whether UI/UX has a future.

**Not covered in the post or comments:** Electron or desktop support.

The docs don't describe a viewer UI or an `e2e show-report` command. The report is files you open yourself.

- **Failing run:** The `list` reporter prints the error, the failing line, nearby locator matches, the app's error count, and a path to the test's `trace.md`. Open the trace in an editor's markdown preview so its links work.
- **Passing run:** No trace is written by default. `--trace` keeps one for every test, and `--trace off` writes none. The `markdown` reporter writes `.e2e/summary.md`, and `report.json` holds every result.
- **Step-through:** The trace lists each step with its duration, the node it acted on, assertion readings, replay-cache decisions, app log entries, page navigations, and screen changes since the previous step. `report.json` has the same step data.
- **Screenshots:** Not captured per step. They come from failed attempts when the engine can take one, from `agent.assert` after either verdict, and from `app.screenshot()` calls. The trace embeds the failure screenshot and a semantic tree of the screen.
- **Video:** Enabled with `--video`, optionally with a mode such as `retain-on-failure`. Each page gets a WebM file on web or an MP4 on a device. To find a step in the video, subtract the recording's `startedAt` from the step's `startedAt`.
- **Agent reasoning:** The trace shows the agent's last turns. `--debug` adds a per-step timing and token table and saves model transcripts as artifacts. `--ai-trace` writes `.e2e/ai-trace.json`, which you read with the separate unbox-ai tool.

The `web()` options documented here are below. Several options you asked about (launch args, `executablePath`, `channel`, `userDataDir`, `wsEndpoint`, extensions, and storage state) are not in this page.

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `browser` | Browser to launch: `chromium` (default), `firefox`, or `webkit`, or a `BrowserProvider` that leases hosted browsers. |
| `viewport` | Initial viewport of each attempt's page; defaults to 1280×720, and `null` fills the browser window. |
| `screencast` | Frame size and JPEG quality for the engine's own video recording. |
| `connect` | Attaches to a remote browser over CDP via `cdpEndpoint`, with optional `reconnectEndpoint` for recovery. |
| `headers` | Extra request headers added to requests within the app's site, including subdomains. |
| `basicAuth` | Username and password the browser sends in answer to HTTP 401 challenges. |
| `testIdAttribute` | Attribute that carries test IDs; defaults to `data-testid`. |
| `userAgent` | `User-Agent` string sent by every attempt and reported by `navigator.userAgent`. |

| `initScripts` | Scripts that run in every document before the page's own, given as a string, a file path, or a function. |

**Notes on the options you asked about:**

- **Launch args, `executablePath`, `channel`, `userDataDir`, `wsEndpoint`, extensions:** not documented as `web()` options.
- **Persistent context:** there is no `userDataDir`. A persistent context comes from `connect.reconnectEndpoint` or a provider with `scope: 'attempt'`. It rejects `headers`, `basicAuth`, `userAgent`, `locale`, and `timezoneId`.
- **Storage state:** not a `web()` option. Sessions carry over through a saved session or a sign-in setup test. Persistent contexts don't support session state capture or restore.
- **Hosted providers:** passed as `browser: provider`, leased per worker slot or per attempt. A provider implies chromium and cannot be combined with `connect`. The page refers to a separate hosted-browsers section for the provider contract, which this excerpt does not include.

title: Security
description: What the model can see and do, how secrets stay out of it, and what you still need to watch.
icon: "shield-halved"
"og:image": "https://e2e.tester.army/docs/images/og/security.png?v=6c43d95c56"
"twitter:image": "https://e2e.tester.army/docs/images/og/security.png?v=6c43d95c56"

e2e trusts the code you write and treats everything the app shows as
untrusted. App content can't grant the model tools, credentials, or a
larger budget.

## How secrets stay out of the model

A `Secret` is a handle with no plaintext accessor. The model sees only its
name and purpose. When the model asks to fill one, the runner checks the
field and types the value itself.

After a secret fill, the model gets no screenshots for the rest of the
attempt, because the app could show the value anywhere. Every known secret value becomes
`<secret:name>` in model input, reports, console output, and `.txt`,
`.csv`, `.json`, `.html`, and `.htm` downloads.

## What can still leak

Redaction matches strings, and only a secret fill turns model screenshots off:

- **Screenshots, video, and downloads.** Screenshots mask secure fields
  only, video masks nothing, and a download other than a redacted text file
  is kept as served. If the test typed a password, check them before you
  share them.
- **`command.log`.** It holds your app's stdout and stderr verbatim. Keep
  secrets out of your app's output.
- **Transformed values.** The last four characters of a key, or its base64,
  pass through. Assert the outcome, not the secret.
- **Values not filled as a secret.** A secret passed as a plain string, or a
  sign-in that sets a cookie, leaves model screenshots on. Only a configured
  secret's value is redacted.
- **Request credentials.** `basicAuth` answers a `401` from any origin.
  `headers` reach every host under a shared domain such as `vercel.app`.
- **Committed recordings.** Cache entries store typed values verbatim, except
  secret fills. They aren't signed and replay with your permissions, so
  review them as you would test code.

[Where redaction stops](/reference/security#where-redaction-stops) lists
every case.

## What the model sees and does

The model sees your instruction, the screen as an accessibility tree, the
redacted URL, and records of earlier steps in the test. It gets a masked
screenshot when it asks for one or a step sets `vision`.

The model acts only through tools. The runner checks each call against a
closed schema before it runs, and never evaluates model text as code. A call
that breaks a rule, such as a navigation to `file:`, fails with
`POLICY_DENIED`. There is no origin allowlist: the agent can follow the app
to another site and use the step's secrets there.
